correctness.rationale: A read prefix has residual output a+s_2(v+d) modulo m. Exact transitions retain all reachable d/a pairs; equal d with different a differ on empty input, while unequal d are separated by suffix v=2^L-e, since the digit-sum difference is L-s_2(e-d-1)-1 and therefore cannot stay constant modulo m. Positive-carry states stabilize at depth ceil(log_2(c+1)); all m zero-carry residues occur. Thus the finite-set count is both attainable and a lower bound. At c=2^r each positive-carry depth has min(h+1,m) distinct residues. Independent Moore minimization, direct bit-sum outputs and finite-set enumeration passed on 1032 parameter pairs and 132096 direct inputs. No finite experiment was used as proof of the general formula.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected 2025 source handles shifts of the parity Thue--Morse word with most-significant-first input, yielding a linear upper bound rather than the present exact least-significant-first count for all output moduli. The 2021 Thue--Morse set theorem handles multiplication followed by translation of a set, not shifts of a multi-output digit-sum sequence; the 2026 Fibonacci work uses Zeckendorf representation and a different sequence. Known exact parity-only instances do not determine the modulus-dependent residue saturation, and the elementary carry construction is not itself a minimality theorem. Literature and equivalent-representation searches found no theorem whose hypotheses imply all the present parameters; possible unindexed coverage remains the principal residual risk.
residual_risks: A general carry/transducer theorem in a textbook or unindexed source may imply the state formula without matching its phrasing.
The full 2021 paper was not exhaustively inspected beyond its stated object and opening text, although its declared operation and the 2025 comparison are structurally distinct.
Independent external literature-priority verification has not been performed.

value.rationale: All-shift exact minimal-state counts and an explicit finite invariant answer a natural automata-minimization question, not merely whether the sequence is automatic. The dyadic formula shows a sharp change of growth with the output modulus and gives a closed staircase family. The proof identifies a stable zero-carry component and separates every positive-carry residual, a useful structural reduction independent of finite computation. No downstream theorem is claimed or required.
